messages.subject: error using the ou covariate structure
messages.subject_clean: error using the ou covariate structure
messages.body_plain:
Hey
I´m having tracking data for a year, with one position per day and 4 individuals.
I have a presence/absence column with 1 as present and 0 as absent. In addition, I have variables such as NDVI, precipitation and temp, centred and scaled. Because I have autocorrelation in my data and I'm missing a few dates I want to use the ou covariate to account for this. My model looks like this :
Mod2<- glmmTMB(presence~ NDVI_Sc + temp_Sc + Pres_Sc
               +(1|individual.local.identifier)
               + ou(Date+0| individual.local.identifier),
               data = dat, family = binomial)

This is not working and I get an error message saying :
Error in parseNumLevels(reTrms$cnms[[i]]) : Failed to parse numeric levels: Date In addition: Warning message: In lapply(strsplit(tmp, ","), as.numeric) : NAs introduced by coercion

Interestingly, when I use the Ar1 function, it is working
 + ar1(as.factor(Date)+0| individual.local.identifier),

I have also tried ou(as.factor(Date)+0 but it is not working. I don't understand what's wrong and wonder if someone can explain this issue.
Thank you so much
Kindly
Caka

messages.subject: Finding a stable version of R, TMB etc
messages.subject_clean: Finding a stable version of R, TMB etc
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I am really stuck.

Many researchers at IHME use TMB for large models in R. They have been using the following set of versions for some time because we have not been able to find another set that “works:”

R  3.6
TMB 1.7.16
The symbolic analysis fix
Gcc 4.7
Linux

I could get a more precise version set if you need it, although due to a lost backup I don’t have the dockerfile for this image.

We build a docker image from a docker file, and then convert to a singularity image, and run it on our Ubuntu/Slurm cluster.

We need the speed-optimization provided by runSymbolicAnalysis (RSA)so that our models converge in a practical amount of time. The test model I use converges in 73 minutes using the above configuration. Without RSA it is still running after 24 hours, when I deliberately time it out.

I have been able to build images that “work” (meaning that they don’t stop with an error) using later versions of R and TMB, but I have never been able to find a set of versions where our test model converges, or that work with RSA

My latest attempt:

R 4.2.3
TMB 1.9.4 (which I believe is the latest)
RSA
The gnu threading libraries. I tried Intel’s TBB library but could not get past a missing symbol error.

I can provide a Dockerfile for this version. When I ran our test model it errored after 8.5 hours with a division by zero error in Newton’s method.

Can someone please provide me with a set of versions that works? Or advice? Otherwise we will be stuck on R 3.6 and TMB 1.7.16

Cheers

Geoff

messages.subject: Re: Conceptual question - optimizing model speed / efficiency
messages.subject_clean: Conceptual question - optimizing model speed / efficiency
messages.body_plain:
Without going too much into details: You should code it the way you find easiest - it won't be faster to pass e.g. x^2 rather than x.

On Thursday, July 27, 2023 at 8:29:15 PM UTC+2 pthomp...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Hope everyone's doing well. I have a general question about how to organize my data objects for a TMB function in a way that will allow the function (and of course its gradient) to execute most efficiently. I will try my best at providing a "minimal working example" but this is less of a "my code isn't working problem" and more of a "how do I design / specify / organize things in an optimal way" problem. My indecision here probably comes from a fairly surface-level understanding of automatic differentiation so please pardon that.
>
> Basically, let's say I have some DATA_VECTOR(x) that represents the value of a covariate for many observations. For simplicity let's assume our model only depends on this one covariate, and that there are many observations (i.e., making sure the function and gradient evaluate as quickly as possible is very important). Let's assume that our hypothetical response variable, DATA_VECTOR(y) depends on x in a fairly complex and nonlinear way (i.e., y ~= b1 * x + b2 * x^2 + b3 * exp(x), where b1, b2, b3 are parameters, or something).
>
> The most concise way I can ask my question is, "Should I transform x beforehand and include the transformed versions as separate data arguments, or should I apply the transformations inside the TMB function?". To me, it seems like the former may be faster, because then the TMB function doesn't have to evaluate x^2 every single time (it would already be given x^2 and exp(x) through hypothetical DATA_VECTOR objects, or even a DATA_MATRIX). But I also wonder if, particularly with large datasets, including all these DATA_VECTORs (or a DATA_MATRIX with many rows) could cause memory issues of some kind. Like I said, I'm no expert here, just asking and inquiring.
>
> I realize the answer to this question may depend on details I have not provided (e.g., how big actually is the dataset, or how complex are the functions I'm actually applying to x), so if more information is needed, please let me know. Hopefully this is within the scope of this Google Group; I realize it's not a typical "I have an error and need help" sort of problem. Any insight at all is welcome. Thank you!
>
> Peter R. Thompson

messages.subject: CRAN Note: "Found no calls to: 'R_registerRoutines', 'R_useDynamicSymbols'"
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm trying to submit a package to CRAN that uses TMB.  When running `devtools::check(.)` I get a "Note":

❯ checking compiled code ... NOTE
  File 'phylosem/libs/x64/phylosem.dll':
    Found no calls to: 'R_registerRoutines', 'R_useDynamicSymbols'

There is extensive discussion online involving rstan or Rcpp, and perhaps some evidence that other packages using TMB have found work-arounds (e.g., glmmTMB here <https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/blob/master/glmmTMB/src/init.h#L4-L17>).

Does anyone have any minimal fix for addressing this?

Jim
